method: ig-viral outlier method on YouTube as the main corpus (Instagram had no usable public reel URLs from web search, see confidence). 102 Indian gaming creators listed (BGMI, Free Fire, Valorant, CS2, LoL, Hindi let's-play, co-op horror, clip editors, shorts-first meme channels; 3K to 53M subs). One paced yt-dlp --flat-playlist request per channel tab (Shorts; long-form for 26 channels), 2.5 to 3 s apart, no parallel requests, no login. 92 channels returned usable view counts (3,905 videos). Each video's outlier multiple = views / that channel's own median for that format (Shorts and long-form measured separately). Rows from channels with a median under 1,000 views are kept in the creator table but excluded from formula statistics (3,785 videos remain). Hook = the title (hook_source 'title'): YouTube's bot wall ('Sign in to confirm you're not a bot') blocked per-video metadata after 11 videos, so captions, upload dates and Short lengths were not fetched for the rest and we did not work around it. captured.tsv (587 rows: every >=3x video plus the two lowest per channel-format as the floor) was run through ig-viral/swipe.py -> brain/research/viral/gaming_swipe.md. Because swipe.py named only 56 of 587 hooks with the 26 ig-reel formulas, hooks (titles with hashtags stripped) were also classified with 13 gaming-specific G-formulas (regex, priority order G11 > G13 > G7 > G4 > G5 > G2 > G9 > G3 > G8 > G1 > G10 > G12, else G6 if 4 words or fewer) and compared top third vs bottom third by multiple, per format. Profiles: 15 small-to-mid creators closest to Srijan's lane scored against ig-profile/rubric.json from public channel pages and web-search snippets only; 5 rubric items (pinned, highlights, photo, recent activity, stories) are not observable without opening Instagram and are left null. Copy the formula, never the video: every row is attributed.

sample.date_range: Last 40 uploads per channel (Shorts tab, plus the long-form tab for 26 channels), collected 27 Oct 2026. Flat listings carry no dates; the 11 outliers we could date run 2023-08-04 to 2026-08-27, and feed depth ranges from about 3 weeks (daily posters) to 2+ years (rare posters). Position in the feed (0 = newest) is used as the recency proxy.

formulas.name: Viewer Task CTA
formulas.note: Joint-best hit rate in Shorts with G13: 10 of 32 cleared 3x (31%). Short imperative that gives the viewer a job (tag, comment, guess). GodNixon 'Tag Your Squad' 169x. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 10/32, long 0/8.

formulas.name: Desi Pop-Culture Mashup
formulas.note: A cartoon, cricket, Bollywood or anime reference dropped into a game. 13 of 41 Shorts cleared 3x (32%), 21 in the top third vs 10 in the bottom, and it owns the extreme top (Dragon Ball 600x, Shizuka 160x, RRR 57x, RCB 44x). Recognition does the hook's work. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 13/41, long 1/29.

formulas.name: Big-Name Crossover
formulas.note: Another big creator's name or a collab in the title. 17% hit rate in Shorts; flat in long-form. Borrowed audience, needs access Srijan does not have yet. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 19/109, long 5/109.

formulas.name: Cryptic Micro-Caption
formulas.note: Two to four words, usually a reaction ('bro is gone', 'Emergency', 'game over'). Largest single bucket; slightly over-indexes up top (278 vs 238). Only works when the first frame is the payoff. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 96/770, long 4/63.

formulas.name: Skill Flex Number
formulas.note: A number or a skill claim (1v5, 999 IQ, clutch, ace). Mild over-index in Shorts (53 vs 41). Hit rate >=3x: shorts 19/141, long 1/34.

formulas.name: Rage / Troll / Expose
formulas.note: Rage, troll, expose, toxic, roast. The best long-form formula: 35 top vs 14 bottom, 18% hit rate (SauraXD 'Making Gamer Girls Cry', ytRish Mumbai-server toxicity, kevvv 'This Streamer Made Fun Of Me'). Neutral in Shorts. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 12/93, long 13/71.

formulas.name: Gamer-Life Relatable
formulas.note: 'How gamers...', 'When...', IRL. Under-indexes in Shorts (35 top vs 56 bottom) as a title, even though one of the biggest hits (Chapati 28x) is this shape. The shape is everywhere, so on its own it is noise. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 17/131, long 4/25.

formulas.name: Wait-For-It Payoff
formulas.note: 'Wait for end', 'phir dekho kya hua'. Under-indexes (33 vs 47). Overused by Free Fire skit channels. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 16/129, long 0/6.

formulas.name: Absurd Premise / Can X Do Y
formulas.note: 'Can X...', survive, escape, tries, challenge. Even in Shorts; dead in long-form (1 of 124 cleared 3x) because it is the default long-form title. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 11/84, long 1/124.

formulas.name: Desi Server / Lobby
formulas.note: India, Indian, Mumbai server, desi, random teammates. About baseline (14% in Shorts, 3% in long-form; it is the niche's default), but it is the title of almost every small Valorant/CS2 outlier (ytRish 14x, Lmaoo Noob 10x, Salty Boys 3.7x). Hit rate >=3x: shorts 6/44, long 4/132.

formulas.name: Friend Callout
formulas.note: A friend or teammate named in the title (@mention, dost, squad, bhai). Slightly under baseline (8% in Shorts, 44 top vs 53 bottom); works only when the friend is a known character (NotGamerFleet's @GamerFleet 26x). Hit rate >=3x: shorts 13/153, long 2/31.

formulas.name: News / Drop / Event
formulas.note: News, drops, events: GTA 6, PMWC/EWC/BGIS, bundles, updates. Baseline overall; small esports-news channels spike on fresh results (iFlicks 22x, Droid Plays 22-24x). Hit rate >=3x: shorts 17/135, long 0/26.

formulas.name: Series Label
formulas.note: Part / Episode / Day N. Never cleared 3x (0 of 47). Bottom-heavy in long-form (3 top vs 26 bottom). Series labels hold a base, they do not break out. Hit rate >=3x: shorts 0/11, long 0/36.

formulas.name: The 26 ig-reel formulas
formulas.note: swipe.py named only 56 of 587 captured hooks with the 26 formulas (531 unclassified). Classified hooks sit more in the bottom third (24) than the top (16). Head To Head (#17, 'PUBG vs Free Fire') x5 and Verbatim Question (#16, 'Can ACP play Among Us?') x4 were the only repeats in the top third. Indian gaming titles are not written in the education/business hook grammar the 26 come from, which is why the G-series above exists. Median hook score top third 29 vs bottom 31: hookscore.py does not separate gaming titles.

structure: Shorts break out, long-form holds: 12% of Shorts cleared 3x their channel median vs 5% of long videos (2,661 vs 1,124 videos).

The title barely separates winners from losers in Shorts: median title length is 5 words in both the top and bottom third, and hookscore.py gives the top third 29 vs 31 for the bottom. In Shorts the first frame is the hook; the title is a caption. This data cannot see the first frame.

What the top-third Shorts titles do have: a reaction in 4 words or fewer (14% hit rate vs 11%), Roman Hinglish (15% vs 12%), an @mention of a known person (16% vs 12%), one or two emoji with 💀 or 🤣. ALL-CAPS titles (9% vs 13%) and pipe-separated series titles (5% vs 13%) under-index.
Long-form is the opposite: the top third is driven by conflict words (rage, troll, toxic, expose, roast: 18% hit rate) and the 'Part / Episode / Day N' label never broke out (0 of 36).

Age effect: top-third Shorts sit deeper in the feed (median position 20 vs 15), so part of every multiple is time to accumulate views. Outliers among a channel's last five uploads (listed in viral_now) are the cleaner signal.

Channel size: channels under 100K subs hit 3x on 9% of Shorts vs 13 to 14% for bigger channels, but the biggest multiples in the whole set come from small or mid channels (Half Skirmish 271x on a 354 median, THELEGENDSHREEMAAN 302x on 4,300, GodNixon 169x on 39,000).

Known lengths (11 dated outliers): the big Shorts hits are 16 to 59 s, most 16 to 35 s (GodNixon 16 s and 35 s, THELEGENDSHREEMAAN 22 s, LUCIFER DANGE 25 s, PHOENIX 29 s). The long-form outlier (JerryVirus REPO highlights) is 12:47.

CTA: the only CTA that shows up as a title pattern is the viewer task (tag your squad, comment, guess). It ties with G13 for the best hit rate in the set (31 to 32%). No other CTA is visible from titles.

doesnt: Topic alone. GTA 6 titles (111 videos) have a median multiple of 0.96x and 6% cleared 3x; R.E.P.O. 0.96x; Backrooms 0.86x; horror/scary/haunted words 0.95x with 3% over 3x. Everyone in the niche covers these, so the topic is the baseline, not the lift.
Series labels: Part / Episode / Day N cleared 3x 0 times in 47 videos and sit in the bottom third of long-form (26 bottom vs 3 top). They keep a base audience; they never break out.
'Wait for end' / 'phir dekho kya hua' bait: 33 top vs 47 bottom in Shorts. Free Fire skit channels have worn it out.

Generic 'How gamers... / When... / Every gamer...' titles: 35 top vs 56 bottom in Shorts. The relatable shape only works when the clip itself is specific (Chapati 'How gamers solve problems' 28x is the exception, not the rule).
ALL-CAPS Shorts titles (9% vs 13%) and pipe-separated SEO titles on Shorts (5% vs 13%).

Business-style hook grammar: the 26 ig-reel formulas named only 56 of 587 hooks, and the named ones sit more in the bottom third (24) than the top (16). hookscore.py does not separate gaming titles (29 top vs 31 bottom).

Long-form for very small channels: Salty Boys' long-form median is 3,000 and JerryVirus' 1,250; their Shorts medians are 1,500 and 15,000. JerryVirus' 98K REPO highlights (78x) shows a long video can pop, but it took 40 uploads to find one.

COD MW4 and LoL: zero Indian creators in the 92 channels titled a video about either in their last 40 uploads (3 old COD titles in total). There is no Indian evidence for these yet, only the global trend.

R.E.P.O. / Mimic-style co-op chaos with the same 3 to 4 friends, titled as a viewer task ('Tag the friend who...') (G11 on co-op footage). Why: G11 has a joint-best hit rate in the set (31%) and the tag turns the clip into a share inside friend groups like his own; co-op party games with friends are the hottest topic shape right now (Mimic 2.0x median).

Desi pop-culture lines said in his own voice over his own clips: a monster becomes 'Shinchan ki mummy', Backrooms Level 0 becomes 'Pune PG ka corridor' (G13). Why: recognition is the biggest lift in the data (32% hit rate, 13 of 41, and the top of the table), and saying the reference himself avoids copyrighted clips and fits his Hinglish voice.

First-person Hinglish inner-monologue captions about office-gamer life (candidate formula from the unclassified rows). Why: Neyoo 36x and GodNixon 17x show the 'socha ki...' shape works, and it is exactly how Srijan already talks (self-roast first, short verdict last). His 9-to-6 job is the angle nobody in this sample has.

Micro-captions of 4 words or fewer with 💀 on a clip whose first frame is already the payoff (G6). Why: 14% hit rate and the biggest recent BGMI hits (GodNixon 'bro is gone 💀' 138x at 16 s); it only works if the edit starts on the moment, which suits his setup-to-payoff-under-20-s lane.

'Before GTA 6' as a joke line, not GTA 6 news. Why: GTA 6 titles are saturated (0.96x), but the meme form still lifts (Chapati 'iPhone 18 before GTA 6' 7.3x, Mythpat 'First Indian To Buy GTA 6' 4.1x). He has no console for launch day, so the joke is the only GTA 6 content he can make.

A Diwali (8 Nov) 'gamer's Diwali' mini-vlog Short: rig, Sophie, patakhe, friends online. Why: both festival Shorts in the sample beat their channel by 7.8x to 8.8x last year, and it bridges his gaming and Pune/personality pillars.

Later, not now: long-form compilations with a conflict title ('My friends sold me out 4 times in R.E.P.O.'). Why: G4 is the only long-form formula that over-indexes, but small channels' long-form medians are a fraction of their Shorts; build the Shorts base first.

Not observable without opening Instagram (left null in every breakdown): pinned three, highlights, profile photo, posting recency and story rings. Scores are out of the 60 observable points, scaled to 100.

confidence: Medium on the shape findings, low on timing. 3,785 videos across 89 channels with medians of 1,000+ (3,905 across 92 in total) is a real sample for 'what over-indexes': G11 Viewer Task (10/32 over 3x), G13 Pop-Culture Mashup (13/41), G4 in long-form (13/71) and the Part/Episode null result (0/47) are findings; most other G-formulas sit within a few points of the 12% Shorts baseline and are not. Limits: (1) hooks are titles, not the spoken first line or the first frame; YouTube's bot wall stopped per-video fetches after 11 videos and captions were not attempted, so the visual hook (what actually decides a Short) is unmeasured. (2) Only 11 outliers are dated; 'viral now' leans on feed position and on brain/research/reports/2026-10-27.md, so treat the 'until' dates as estimates. (3) Multiples include an age effect (older videos had longer to grow). (4) Instagram: web search returned no public reel URLs for these creators (only profile pages, which we did not open), so the Instagram corpus is zero and profile scores use YouTube pages plus search snippets; 40 of 100 rubric points are unobservable. (5) G-formula matching is regex on Hinglish titles and will misfile some rows; 788 Shorts stayed unclassified. (6) Few accounts are within 10x of Srijan's size (928 IG followers); the closest are Salty Boys, Lmaoo Noob, RishYT, No Pressure, BerzereX, Half Skirmish.
